## 4. Findings

1. **Explainable from valid inputs; no implementation error found.** The feature contributions add up exactly to the prediction, the clay Elo matches the rating engine, and the most recent results are released on the snapshot day by the same rule used in training.
2. **Clay Elo does favour Alcaraz** (2035 vs 1993) and pushes -0.096 toward him. Model D learned (2015-2024) to weigh general Elo more than surface Elo, and general Elo favours Sinner by 70 points (+0.227). Net Elo group: +0.131.
3. **Activity is the largest single driver** (rest/workload +0.271 of the +0.434 total). Alcaraz has no recorded match after the tournament starting 2026-04-13: 0 matches in the last 30 days and 8 in 90, against 2 and 25 for Sinner. Historically, players coming off a gap or a light schedule did worse. **The data does not record why a player stopped** (injury, rest, scheduling). That is the most important missing information here: for a precautionary break the model may overstate the effect; for an injury it may understate it.
4. **Form nearly cancels out in Model D** (all form groups together +0.021). Decayed and opponent-adjusted form favour Sinner, raw win-rate windows push back. These features are strongly correlated, so single signs are not meaningful; read the group total.
5. **Head-to-head is not a Model D input.** Alcaraz leads the recorded meetings; V2's shrunk H2H residual is small (-0.098) because 17 meetings are weak evidence next to thousands of other matches.
6. **Serve and return favour Sinner.** V2 sees a clearly stronger recent serve (clay serve rating +0.115 vs +0.055) and equal return. The raw matchup model says 77.7%, but it is overconfident (calibration slope 0.69 on the reporting folds); the diagnostic V2 LR says 66.1%. V2 does not move the estimate toward Alcaraz.
7. **Not available:** court conditions for a specific venue, weather, fitness or injury reports, and match dates. None was invented.

**Conclusion.** The 60.7% is a consequence of valid inputs, not a bug. The counterintuitive part (a higher clay Elo outweighed) comes from general Elo and, above all, Alcaraz's absence in the data. The honest caveat is that the model cannot tell an injury from a planned rest. A future V2 stage should model absences explicitly and use documented withdrawal or injury data if a licensed source provides it.

| Model D | 60.7% | 1.65 | 2.54 |
| V2 LR (diagnostic) | 66.1% | 1.51 | 2.95 |
| V2.1 LR (diagnostic) | 61.4% | 1.63 | 2.59 |

**Calibration evidence relevant to this case (dev 2023-2024, post hoc, descriptive):** in 852 matches where only the underdog had been inactive for 45+ days, Model D gave the favourite 71.8% on average and favourites won 69.4%. That suggests the models lean slightly too far toward the active player, which is the Sinner side here. It is a hypothesis for a pre-registered test, not a correction: no prediction was adjusted.

**Reading.** Most of the gap comes from the features V2.1 adds, not from regularisation. Its workload term (sets in the last 30 days) and points-vs-expectation terms overlap with inputs V2 already has (match counts, recent serve/return ratings), so the fit splits the same evidence differently between correlated columns. On thousands of matches the two splits score the same (log loss 0.6097 vs 0.6098); on one extreme case they can differ by several points. This is ordinary model uncertainty, not an error in either model.

## 7. Checks before integration

**Service-return (Markov) model.** Points are treated as independent with a fixed serve-win chance per player; games, 7-point tiebreak sets and best of 3 or 5 follow the official scoring. The final set is treated as a normal tiebreak set: since 2022 the Slams play a 10-point tiebreak at 6-6 in the final set, a small approximation. The format is the user's choice in the app (best of 3 by default, best of 5 for Slams). The result does not depend on who serves first (tested), and inputs outside 30%-95% are clipped. Here: Sinner wins 64.1% of his serve points and Alcaraz 58.1% (clay tour average 61.8%).

**Statistics at the snapshot.** Sinner has 442 and Alcaraz 368 released matches with serve/return statistics. Of 445 active players, 86 have none (V2 returns 'unavailable' for them) and 141 have fewer than 10 (V2 shows a warning).

**Production artifact.** artifacts/v2.pkl refits the frozen V2 settings on all approved data (to tournaments starting 2026-05-25); for Sinner vs Alcaraz on clay, best of 3, it gives **68.5%** (the 66.1% above is the 2015-2024 research fit).
